status: rule-generated from the niqqud text; not verified by a native speaker; no audio exists
description: How the SSML strings in the _ssml shards are built and what is known about using them. NOT tested against any engine.

format.separator: one space between words; maqaf also becomes a space
format.ph: IPA with syllable dots removed, primary stress mark ˈ kept before the stressed syllable

israeli.ipaInventory: b v ɡ d h z χ t j k l m n s p f ts ʁ ʃ + a e i o u; no ʔ or ʕ written; stress final unless a listed exception
israeli.browser: the only tradition a stock he-IL browser voice approximates; use the pointed Hebrew text, not the IPA

sephardi.ipaInventory: adds ʔ (aleph), ħ (het), ʕ (ayin), trilled r, x; no length marks
sephardi.browser: no browser voice is known to do this; the he-IL voice will read it as Israeli. Needs a recording or an engine that honours IPA

ashkenazi.ipaInventory: adds ɔ (kamatz), ej (tzere), oj (cholam), s for tav without dagesh, x, r, ə final; penultimate stress
ashkenazi.browser: no browser voice is known to do this; same caveat as Sephardi

engines: The Web Speech API (speechSynthesis) generally takes plain text and ignores SSML markup, so the phoneme elements are for server-side engines or a future TTS lane that documents <phoneme alphabet="ipa">. Which engines accept he-IL with IPA, and whether they honour ħ ʕ ɔ, has NOT been checked here.
fallbackText: For the Web Speech API pass `words[].h` joined by spaces (pointed Hebrew) with lang he-IL, Israeli tradition only.
warnings: Phoneme strings are rule output, not verified by a native speaker.
An engine that silently ignores unknown IPA will read the Hebrew text in its own way: compare against the recording before relying on it.
